subject: maths
title: KS3 Maths diagnostic
curriculum: National Curriculum in England, key stage 3 mathematics programme of study (2013)

skills.name: Number
skills.why: Strong number skills make every other part of maths quicker and more accurate.
skills.strong: {name} calculates confidently, including negative numbers and standard form.
skills.developing: {name} is secure with written calculation but less sure with negative numbers and factors.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet secure with written calculation and number facts. Everything else in KS3 builds on this, so it comes first.
skills.next_step: We will strengthen calculation and number facts with short, regular practice.

skills.name: Fractions, percentages and ratio
skills.why: Fractions, percentages and ratio are used constantly at GCSE and in everyday life.
skills.strong: {name} works confidently with fractions, percentages and proportion.
skills.developing: {name} understands equivalent fractions but finds comparing values and percentage change harder.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet confident with fractions and percentages. These carry a lot of weight at GCSE, so they are worth securing now.
skills.next_step: We will use visual models to make fractions and percentages click.

skills.name: Algebra
skills.why: Algebra is the biggest part of GCSE maths, and KS3 is where the foundations are laid.
skills.strong: {name} solves equations and works with sequences and brackets confidently.
skills.developing: {name} can substitute into expressions but finds solving equations and sequences harder.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet confident with the basics of algebra. Getting this right now makes GCSE much easier.
skills.next_step: We will build algebra step by step, starting from substitution and simple equations.

skills.name: Geometry and measures
skills.why: Geometry builds spatial reasoning and gives dependable marks in every exam.
skills.strong: {name} works confidently with angles, volume, circles and Pythagoras.
skills.developing: {name} is secure with angles and volume but less sure with circles and right-angled triangles.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet secure with angle facts and measuring shapes. These come up constantly, so they are worth practising now.
skills.next_step: We will practise the key angle facts and formulas with plenty of examples.

skills.name: Statistics and probability
skills.why: Reading data and thinking about chance are skills used in science, geography and everyday life.
skills.strong: {name} calculates averages and probabilities and reads charts confidently.
skills.developing: {name} handles averages well but is less sure with pie charts and probability.
skills.gap: {name} is not yet confident with averages and probability. These are quick wins, so we can make progress fast.
skills.next_step: We will work through averages, charts and probability with short, clear methods.

questions.stem: Work out 1000 − 358
questions.explain: 1000 − 358 = 642. Check: 642 + 358 = 1000. Errors here usually come from exchanging across the zeros.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
questions.explain: Multiply top and bottom by 2: 6/8. 4/5 adds 1 to each part.

questions.stem: If a = 4, what is the value of 3a + 2?
questions.explain: 3 × 4 + 2 = 14. 36 comes from reading 3a as 34.

questions.stem: Two angles sit together on a straight line. One of them is 125°. What is the other angle?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°: 180 − 125 = 55°. 235 uses 360.

questions.stem:
What is the range of these numbers?
4, 11, 7, 2, 9
questions.explain: Range = largest − smallest = 11 − 2 = 9.

questions.stem: A cuboid measures 5 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 cm³. 12 adds the lengths.

questions.stem: A fair spinner has 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5. What is the probability of spinning an even number?
questions.explain: Even numbers are 2 and 4: 2 out of 5. 1/2 assumes half of all numbers are even.

questions.ref: Negative numbers and order of operations
questions.stem: Work out −7 + 3 × (−2)
questions.explain: 3 × (−2) = −6, then −7 + (−6) = −13. 8 comes from working left to right and mishandling the signs.

questions.stem:
Put these in order, from smallest to largest:
0.6,  5/8,  62%

questions.ref: Solve equations with unknowns on both sides
questions.stem:
Solve 5x − 4 = 2x + 11

What is the value of x?
questions.explain: Subtract 2x: 3x − 4 = 11. Add 4: 3x = 15. So x = 5.

questions.stem:
Find the mean of these numbers:
6, 8, 10, 12, 14
questions.explain: Total 50, divided by 5 = 10.

questions.stem: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 120?
questions.explain: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 120 = 2³ × 3 × 5. Common: 2² × 3 = 12. 6 and 4 are common factors but not the highest.

questions.stem: A recipe for 4 people uses 300 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 10 people?
questions.explain: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 g per person, × 10 = 750 g. 306 adds 6.

questions.stem:
What is the nth term of this sequence?
7, 11, 15, 19, ...
questions.explain: Goes up by 4, so 4n. 4 × 1 = 4 and the first term is 7, so add 3: 4n + 3. 4n + 7 gives 11 first.

questions.stem: A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. What is its circumference? Use π = 3.14
questions.explain: C = π × d = 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm. 78.5 is the area; 62.8 uses the diameter as the radius.

questions.stem: A class has 12 boys and 18 girls. They are shown on a pie chart. What angle represents the girls?
questions.explain: 18 out of 30 = 3/5. 3/5 × 360° = 216°. 18 is the number, not the angle.

questions.stem: The price of a ticket rises from £40 to £46. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explain: Increase £6. 6 ÷ 40 = 0.15 = 15%. 13% divides by the new price.

questions.stem: Expand and simplify (x + 3)(x − 5)
questions.explain: x² − 5x + 3x − 15 = x² − 2x − 15. x² − 15 misses the middle terms; + 2x gets the sign wrong.

questions.stem: Write 0.00072 in standard form.
questions.explain: Move the decimal point 4 places to get 7.2, so 7.2 × 10⁻⁴. 72 × 10⁻⁵ and 0.72 × 10⁻³ are equal in value but not standard form.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of 5 cm and 12 cm. How long is the longest side?
questions.explain: 5² + 12² = 25 + 144 = 169, and √169 = 13 cm. 17 adds the sides.
